messages:
Samir K.: FYI I hit a tail-latency regression after flipping FlashAttn v3 on staging for short-sequence traffic.
Samir K.: The surprising bit is a spike in GPU memory churn right around KV cache regeneration windows. Attaching quick profiler dump.
PerfBot: auto-profile attached (sampler) — stage-cluster-3 — 3444442000
PerfBot: ````
GPU timeline: 12:34:20 - 12:34:28: high memcpy, repeated small kernels
Hot kernels: flash_attn_v3_forward (70%), kv_cache_regen (18%), memcopy_d2d (8%)
CPU thread: batching_worker_7 stuck at sleep->wake in 3ms loops
Avg latency (p50/p95/p99): 8ms / 65ms / 210ms (baseline v2: 7ms / 18ms / 28ms)
````
Dina L.: Thanks — can you paste the exact flag/commit that enabled v3? Also which workload (seq len distribution + batch target)? :thinking:
Samir K.: Enabled by fflag `runtime.attn.variant=flashv3_auto` (commit ab4c9d2). Traffic: 70% short (<=32), 20% med (33-256), 10% long. Autoscaler batch target = 64 tokens, max_batch_size=128.
Chris P.: My first guess: v3 introduces a KV cache regen path that reallocs or reserializes KV blobs for mixed-length batching; when short sequences dominate, continuous small batches cause frequent partial KV writes -> extra memcopy + kernel launches.
Chris P.: Can we see the batching histogram? If batches frequently end up <8 tokens effective, the kernel overhead kills us.
Jae R.: Query to pull token-length distribution and effective batch sizes (ClickHouse):
Jae R.: ````sql
SELECT seq_len_bucket, count() AS cnt, avg(effective_batch_size)
FROM runtime.requests
WHERE env='staging' AND ts > now() - interval 2 hour
GROUP BY seq_len_bucket
ORDER BY seq_len_bucket
````
Samir K.: Ran it, attaching summary: <=16: 48%, 17-32: 22%, 33-128: 20%, >128: 10%. effective_batch_size avg = 22 for short bucket.
Dina L.: That matches the symptoms. For short-heavy traffic we should either: (A) prefer flashv2 for short batches, (B) tweak v3 to avoid regen on small batches, or (C) change batching heuristic to aggregate tokens differently.
Chris P.: Proposal sketch: add a `kv_regen_threshold` guarded by runtime flag. If effective_batch_tokens < threshold (e.g., 256 tokens), skip the expensive regen path and fall back to the lightweight v2-compatible path. Pseudocode:
Chris P.: ````python
if effective_batch_tokens < FLAGS.kv_regen_threshold:
    use_kernel('flashv2_fallback')
else:
    use_kernel('flashv3_regen')
````
Chris P.: Also add per-pool telemetry counters: regen_skipped_count, regen_triggered_count, avg_regen_membytes.
Samir K.: Sounds good. How safe is adding a fallback kernel? Any correctness differences?
Chris P.: For now, fallback preserves outputs; it's the same matmul path but different blocking. We need to validate numeric parity on 1e-6. I'll run the parity harness.
Dina L.: For rollout: I'd rather gate with a canary routing rule: 5% of short-seq traffic to v3 with regen enabled, 95% to v2/fallback. Observe p95/p99 and mem metrics for 24h. If stable, ramp by 10x.
Samir K.: Can we get automated alerting on regen memory growth? Suggest these alerts:
- alert if avg_regen_membytes > baseline*1.3 for 10m
- alert if regen_skipped_rate > 0.2 for short-bucket (means heuristic misfired)
- alert if p99 latency increases > 2x for short traffic
Jae R.: I'll add queries and dashboards. Dashboard panels: per-kernel GPU time, memcpy time, regen triggers, effective_batch_size heatmap.
PerfBot: Created perf-check job: `perf/attn/kv-regen-canary` — will run 1h window after each deploy and post failure if p99 pokes above threshold.
Samir K.: Action items:
- Chris: implement `kv_regen_threshold` + telemetry (PR target: today EOD)
- Jae: dashboard & alert queries + canary routing rule in TrafficRouter (PR tomorrow)
- Dina: coordinate canary rollout and write runbook steps for rollback
- Samir: run parity + stress harness against quantized models and mixed-batch mode
Dina L.: Small UX note: add an explicit flag `runtime.attn.kv_regen=on|off|auto` so SRE can force-off if needed.
Chris P.: Agree. I'll include that in the PR and add a unit test for the heuristic boundary (threshold +/- 10%).
Samir K.: Thanks. If anyone finds sample traces (perf flamegraphs, nvprof dumps) drop them here. Let's try to keep the initial canary only on staging clusters labelled `stg-canary-3`.
Jae R.: Pushed the dashboard skeleton: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/attn/kv-regen (shared)
Dina L.: lgtm :thumbsup: — after Chris's PR lands we'll coordinate the 5% route and watch perf-check.
Chris P.: PR: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4897 — draft. Contains threshold config + telemetry counters + unit tests.
Samir K.: Great. I'll queue the parity runs and post results in the morning.
Dina L.: Thanks team — high priority since this affects production short-seq latency. :exclamation:
Samir K.: tagging @oncall for awareness.
